title: Selected Crop Management Practises
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 7 Agriculture; not yet checked by a CBC Agriculture teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Carry out gapping, thinning, weeding by hand and earthing-up on the school maize, beans or kale. Thinned seedlings can be transplanted or eaten.

skills.key_step: The child names crop management practices and what each does: gapping (fills spaces), thinning (removes extra seedlings), weeding (removes competition for water, nutrients and light), earthing-up (supports the plant, covers roots and tubers).

floor.prerequisite: Knows how seedlings are cared for after transplanting.
floor.question: What is done when a seedling dies?

representations: a row of seedlings drawn with gaps and crowding

board.do: Draw a row with a gap and a crowded patch.

misconceptions.repair: Grow two rows of beans, one weeded; compare their size after three weeks.
Use the words: thin = make fewer; gap = fill a gap.
Point at an empty space in a row: "a gap" is filled by gapping.

listen_for: Sowing more seeds near the plant
misconceptions.repair: Show earthed-up potatoes and maize; ask what has been added.

checks.question: What is gapping?
checks.answer: replacing seeds or seedlings that failed

checks.question: Why is earthing-up done on potatoes?
checks.answer: to cover the tubers and support the plant

skills.key_step: The child says when and how each practice is done: gap within two weeks with the same crop, thin when moist leaving the strongest, weed before weeds seed and shallowly near the crop, earth up by heaping soil round the stems.
steps: Gap early with the same crop.
Thin in moist soil; keep the strongest.

board.do: Write "maize came up 5 weeks ago; some holes are empty".
Write "gap within two weeks; now it is late".

listen_for: A month or more after germination
misconceptions.repair: Show a late-gapped plant, small beside its neighbours.

misconceptions.ask: Which seedlings are left when thinning?
misconceptions.repair: Compare a big and a weak seedling side by side.

listen_for: When the soil is dry and hard
misconceptions.repair: Pull a seedling from dry soil and from moist soil; look at its neighbours.

listen_for: Dig deep with a jembe right next to the stem
misconceptions.ask: How should weeds close to young maize be removed?
misconceptions.repair: Show cut maize roots after deep weeding close to the stem.

checks.question: Which seedlings are left after thinning?
checks.answer: the strongest ones at the right spacing

checks.question: Why weed before the weeds flower?
checks.answer: so they do not spread seeds
